parents.title: Zero frequency gives residues; square nonzero frequencies create a secondary principal term

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Dualization reveals a hierarchy invisible in the original character average: zero frequency gives the expected diagonal, but arithmetic degeneracy at square nonzero frequencies is coherent enough to survive averaging at main-term scale.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Poisson summation and Gauss sums bridge discriminants to dual frequencies; Euler products and Mellin contours bridge square conditions to residues.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: The proof explicitly applies Poisson summation, separates k=0 from k nonzero, uses G0 to impose the square condition, extracts four residues, and finds additional poles when negative k is a square. The output correctly identifies the square nonzero frequencies as a secondary principal term and notes that the artifact ends at the incomplete R0=R+Q definition.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The proof expands the averaged Aδ,τ expression and applies Lemma 3.6, defining P(l) from k=0 and R0(l) from k≠0. For P(l), G0(ln) vanishes unless ln is a square, reducing n to l1m² and producing residues at ±τ and ±δ. Mellin analysis of R0 shows that when −k is a square, zeta factors have poles at w=±δ, motivating a second main term Q(l).

parents.title: Functional symmetry cancels spurious poles while two-scale bounds control the remainder

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Apparent singularities are artifacts of decomposition. Functional symmetry is the invariant that identifies which residues are structural and which must cancel when the two frequency sectors are recombined.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Euler factorization bridges square dual frequencies to zeta products; the even J-function bridges opposite contours; bilinear averaging bridges large individual remainders to acceptable family error.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: The span factors and analytically continues the secondary series, derives the even J identity, reflects contours, proves individual and bilinear averaged remainder bounds, and explicitly cancels the delta residues between primary and secondary terms. The output correctly states that the averaged remainder estimate is essential and that exact local factors are required for cancellation.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The section factors the square-frequency series H, extends it analytically, derives an identity Jμ,δ(s;l)=Jμ,δ(−s;l), and uses contour reflection to evaluate the secondary principal integral. It proves pointwise and averaged bounds for R(l), the latter through a bilinear lemma and large-sieve estimates, then shows the ±δ residues from P2 cancel those from P, leaving the ±τ main terms of Proposition 2.3.
